Abundant

/uh-BUN-dent/ — rhymes with redundant · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something that is abundant exists in a large quantity, well beyond what is needed.

Berries were so abundant that summer that every family made jam.

Worked Example

The harvest that year was so abundant that farmers filled every barn and still had crops piling up outside.

Abundant captures exactly what happened: not just a large quantity, but a quantity that exceeds what is needed, which is the core meaning. It is more precise than "large" or "plentiful" because it emphasizes the excess beyond necessity.

How Abundant Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

plentiful

plentiful: existing in more than enough supply

ample

ample: generously sufficient for what is needed

profuse

profuse: pouring out freely in great quantity

Antonyms

scarce

scarce: hard to find; in short supply

meager

meager: noticeably small and barely enough

How Strong Is It? — limited → modest → overflowing → abundant

limited vs. abundant

limited vs. abundant: Limited sits at the opposite end of the scale from abundant: a limited supply runs out quickly, while an abundant one goes well beyond what anyone needs.

modest vs. abundant

modest vs. abundant: Modest is much weaker than abundant — a modest amount is respectable but small, while an abundant amount is far more than enough.

overflowing vs. abundant

overflowing vs. abundant: Overflowing is even stronger than abundant: an abundant supply is more than enough, but an overflowing one spills past every container meant to hold it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ab-

Prefix — ab-: off, away from (Latin)

Root — und

Root — und: wave (Latin unda) (Latin)

Suffix — -ant

Suffix — -ant: being in a state of (adjective-forming) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Ab- ('away, off') + und ('wave') + -ant paints a picture of water surging away in waves — something abundant exists in such quantity that it seems to overflow well beyond what is needed.

Use the root in a new word: inundate

Use the root in a new word: inundate: When floodwater inundates a town, it washes over everything in waves — the same Latin root und ('wave') that makes abundant mean overflowing in quantity.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Abundant is the word when you emphasize not just large quantity but quantity exceeding expectation or need. For everyday 'plenty,' simpler words like plentiful work just as well.
